data.narrative:
Koloma is a Series B-stage climate and energy company founded by Tom Darrah, Pete Johnson, and Paul Harraka. The valuation analysis draws on a comparison universe of 9 private peers and 1 public comparable (LNZA), all operating in the Climate & Energy sector at Series B/C stages.

Two triangulation methods were applied. The stage-progression method uses the company's $245M in total raised as a proxy for current value, applying a 1.9x step-up multiplier typical of Series B advancement, yielding $466M. The peer-median method benchmarks against three same-sector, same/adjacent-stage companies: KoBold Metals ($3.0B Series C), Electric Hydrogen ($1.0B Series C), and Amogy ($700M Series C). The median peer valuation is $1.0B, with a range spanning $700M to $3.0B.

The triangulated analysis supports a valuation range of $396M (low) to $1.1B (high), with a median of $733M. The 2.8x spread between low and high reflects material uncertainty inherent to early-stage frontier tech. Key variables driving this range include stage-specific timing assumptions in the progression method and heterogeneity in peer technology maturity and capital efficiency. The peer-median method carries particular weight given the direct comparability of the sample, though the wide dispersion among peers underscores sector-wide valuation volatility in pre-commercialization energy technologies.
